questions.question: A path operation declares a return type annotation and a response_model at the same time. Which of the two does FastAPI use for the response?
questions.expected_answer: The response_model takes priority. FastAPI uses it to do the data validation, documentation, etc. for the response, while the return type annotation remains useful for the editor and tools like mypy.
questions.note: The term response_model occurs across response-model, response-status-code and advanced/additional-responses. Only one short section answers the priority question.

questions.question: How do I build a dependency whose behaviour is configured per path operation, for example a fixed string it compares against?
questions.expected_answer: Use a class with a __call__ method and declare the configuration as parameters of __init__. Create an instance with the values you want and pass that instance to Depends, so each path operation can depend on a differently parameterized instance.
questions.note: tutorial/dependencies/classes-as-dependencies covers classes as dependencies in almost the same words, but instantiates the class per request instead of parameterizing one instance.

questions.question: If I return a Response directly in FastAPI, how can I still document its media type in OpenAPI using response_class?
questions.expected_answer: Returning a Response directly means FastAPI sends it as-is and does not automatically validate, serialize, or document its data. To still document the media type with response_class, declare response_class in the path operation decorator and return your Response object directly. FastAPI uses response_class for OpenAPI documentation, while the returned Response is the one actually sent.
questions.note: The first section states the negative rule: a directly returned Response is not automatically validated, serialized, or documented. The second section gives the response_class-specific workaround: declare response_class for OpenAPI documentation while returning a Response directly at runtime. The question names response_class to exclude the alternative additional-responses mechanism.
